Daily dependency check for this repo. This run never merges a PR and never dismisses or changes a Dependabot alert: a person does that. It may open upgrade PRs (not drafts) and must never push to the default branch.

You are root inside the Box. Install any toolchain you need for live verification; don't skip a live test because a tool is missing. The repo's setup lines and brief come from its moor repo config: don't create or edit `.moor.yaml` and don't open a setup PR. Note anything you installed that setup didn't cover as a proposed setup line.

Make the oursky/os-dev skills available: `npx -y skills add oursky/os-dev -g --skill engineering-audit-deps --skill engineering-review-dependabot`. Check out the default branch and `git pull`. You can't invoke those two skills as slash commands; read each SKILL.md and follow it yourself.

Live tests for this repo: the Docker Compose stack (see the brief: postgres, redis, authgear, api; migrate; login with OTP 111111) and the Android app (build, boot the emulator on /dev/kvm, install, launch, screenshot). The iOS app too: claim a minion and run the simulator there (build, install, launch, screenshot) on base, and on the PR branch if an upgrade touches the app. Run long commands as background jobs; your Bash tool caps a foreground command at 10 minutes. The Box has 16 GB: stop the compose stack before the Android build if memory is short.

How the run goes. moor holds this run open until its gates pass, so finish them in order and call report_step for each with the files it names. moor checks some of those files against GitHub itself, so write them exactly as described (tab-separated, header line first). Never merge a PR, dismiss an alert, approve or review a PR, or comment: a person does that.
1. Gate review. Follow engineering-review-dependabot's SKILL.md with --dry-run=true --dismiss-alerts=false. Approve, merge, comment on and dismiss nothing. Write its full report. Done when: The report lists every open Dependabot PR and alert with what the skill would do. Write dependabot-review.md (the full report) and alerts.tsv: header "repo<TAB>item<TAB>action<TAB>reason", then one row per open Dependabot alert (item = the alert number) and per open Dependabot PR (item = pr<number>), repo as owner/name, action fix, dismiss or person for an alert and merge or skip for a PR, and a reason. moor fails the gate when an open alert or Dependabot PR is missing.
2. Gate audit. Follow engineering-audit-deps's SKILL.md on the default branch. If it makes upgrade commits, push a new branch and open a PR (not a draft) that says it was made by moor's dependency check; if an open PR already covers the upgrade, use that PR's branch. Write the audit table, the PR URL or 'nothing upgraded', and what needs a person's decision. Done when: audit.md has the table and either a PR URL or 'nothing upgraded'. Also write upgrade-prs.txt: one URL per line of each upgrade PR, new or reused, or the single word none. moor checks each one is open against the default branch.
3. Gate live. Run the repo's live tests (see the prompt) on the default branch, then on the PR branch if there is one, so an existing failure can be told apart from a new one. With no PR, run them once on base. Save logs and screenshots, and write a matrix of base vs PR per surface (Docker, Android, iOS) with pass, fail or n/a and timings. Also test each Dependabot PR the review would merge, against base. Then write for-a-person.md: every PR a person could merge and every alert a person could dismiss each with its live result and the review's reason, and mark each PR merge or skip. Do not merge or dismiss anything yourself. Done when: live-matrix.md exists and every surface is pass, fail or n/a with a reason. for-a-person.md lists every candidate with merge or skip. Also write live.tsv: header "surface<TAB>ref<TAB>result<TAB>reason", one row per surface and ref, ref = base or pr<number>, result pass, fail or n/a, and a reason unless pass. Surfaces: docker, android, ios. Every upgrade PR and every Dependabot PR marked merge needs its own rows and a link in for-a-person.md. A failing test is a result, not a reason to stop: record it and go on.
4. Gate report. Write the final summary: what the review would do, upgrades and PR URL or 'nothing upgraded', the live matrix, proposed setup lines, and every place moor got in your way. Add the recommended actions from for-a-person.md as a checklist with links, for a person to merge and dismiss themselves. Done when: The note is the full summary. Write the summary to result.md and call report_step for gate report with the summary as its note: that note is the run's result.
